content.page_title: Right heart catheterization / EMB / Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

recommendations.recommendation: Recommended in patients with severe HF being evaluated for heart transplantation or mechanical circulatory support (MCS).
Should be considered in patients where HF is thought to be due to constrictive pericarditis, restrictive cardiomyopathy, congenital heart disease, and high-output states.
Should be considered in patients with probable pulmonary hypertension (assessed by echo) to confirm diagnosis and assess reversibility before correction of valve/structural disease.
May be considered in selected patients with HFpEF to confirm the diagnosis.
Should be considered in patients with rapidly progressive HF despite standard therapy when there is a probability of a specific diagnosis that can be confirmed only in myocardial samples.

section_5.title: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

subsection_5_1.title: The diagnosis of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
subsection_5_1.content: Diagnosis of HFrEF requires presence of symptoms and/or signs of HF and a reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF <40%). This is most usually obtained by echocardiography.

abbreviations.HFpEF: heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
abbreviations.HFrEF: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
